facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s
weighing 109kg
stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed in November 2013
pulmonary and liver metastases
radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias on his lower right lateral shin
the lesion was not associated with pain or pruritus
Discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels were observed, with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
the epidermis was normal
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R identified as the only somatic mutation

concepts.why: The presence of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels, and a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene are consistent with angiosarcoma.
The appearance of a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque and the absence of pain or pruritus are consistent with cherry angioma, although the size and growth of the lesion are atypical.

The presence of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias and discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels could be consistent with bacillary angiomatosis, although the lack of systemic symptoms and the presence of a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene make this diagnosis less likely.
The appearance of a bright red plaque and the presence of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels are consistent with pyogenic granuloma, although the size and growth of the lesion are atypical.

The presence of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias and discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels could be consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, although the lack of systemic symptoms and the presence of a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's history of stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma and development of a vascular lesion with discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels may be indicative of Cutaneous Angiosarcoma.

rationales.F06: The presence of a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias is more typical of angiosarcoma or cutaneous angiosarcoma.
rationales.F08: The histopathological finding of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels is more characteristic of angiosarcoma or cutaneous angiosarcoma.
rationales.F10: The identification of the KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation is a strong indicator of angiosarcoma or cutaneous angiosarcoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a somatic KDR (VEGFR2) mutation and the patient's history of stage IV cancer support the diagnosis of Cutaneous Angiosarcoma, which is a more specific and severe condition than Angiosarcoma.
